title: Controlled Substance Stewardship policy: the agreed fill interval
content:
**Section 1 — Fill interval set by the agreement.** When the patient signs a new controlled-substance agreement for a controlled prescription of the Prescriptions & Renewals line, the agreement sets the starting fill interval of 14 days. The agreed fill interval is recorded on the prescription as its per-fill days' supply on the day the patient signs, and every later fill of that prescription dispenses that many days.

**Section 2 — How the agreed fill interval is set.** The agreed fill interval is the shortest of five allowances, each a whole number of days worked out on the signing day: the screening allowance, the attendance allowance, the dispensing-regularity allowance, the visit-cadence allowance and the coverage allowance. Each of these allowances is the starting 14 days.

**Section 3 — Effect on later fills.** From the signing day, each fill of the prescription dispenses the agreed fill interval as its days' supply.

**Worked figures (hypothetical signatures).**

| Prescription | Allowances on the signing day | Shortest | Agreed fill interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | 14, 14, 14, 14, 14 | 14 | 14 days |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 14, 14, 14, 14, 14 | 14 | 14 days |

**Points of judgement.**
- The interval is a whole number of days fixed on the signing day.
- The interval is the one figure recorded with the signature as the prescription's per-fill days' supply.
